set.body:
Source: 2026-08-03 quality review. No prior bead; filed because this had no owner.

Problem:
FileJournalControlStore appends every ControlCommand to one file and never reduces it.

- compact (FileJournalControlStore.scala:230-231) trims only the in-memory event cache: value.copy(events = value.events.takeRight(limits.recentEventCacheSize)). It does not touch the file.
- The only channel.truncate (:156) removes a torn trailing record during recovery, not history.
- JournalCommitProbe.checkpoint (:52) is a crash-injection boundary for tests, not a journal checkpoint. The name invites the opposite reading.
- There is no snapshot, rotation, or segment retirement anywhere in the file.

Consequences:
- The journal grows monotonically for the life of the store, including for attempts that reached a terminal state long ago and can never change again.
- replay (:294) reads every record from the beginning on open, so startup cost is proportional to every command ever issued rather than to live attempts. A controller that submits steadily gets slower to start forever, and the cost is paid exactly when recovering from a crash, which is the worst moment for it.
- Disk use has no bound the operator can configure, in a component whose whole purpose is to survive restarts.

Scope, in order:
1. Decide the reduction: periodic snapshot plus a suffix of records, or segment rotation with terminal attempts retired. Snapshot is the smaller change and fits the existing single-file locking.
2. Preserve the guarantees that already hold: atomic replacement, fsync before publication, and torn-tail recovery must all still work if the process dies mid-compaction. A compaction that can lose a committed command is worse than an unbounded file.
3. Give the operator a bound they can set, in JournalLimits alongside recentEventCacheSize.

Acceptance:
- Open cost is proportional to live state plus a bounded suffix, shown by a measured before/after on a journal with a large terminal-attempt history.
- A crash injected at every compaction boundary leaves a journal that replays to the same ControlState, tested the way the existing crash tests inject at commit boundaries.
- Journal size is bounded by configuration.
- Consider renaming JournalCommitProbe.checkpoint once a real checkpoint exists, so the two do not read alike.
set.title: P8.E1: Journal has no on-disk compaction, so open is O(all history)
